changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket. Buy online, return at the till, and the store sees the order, issues the refund and updates the same customer record and loyalty balance. One vendor, one contract, accountable for both. For retail buyers, drop 'unified commerce' and 'point of sale' from customer-facing copy and say 'tills' and 'one system'.
changes.why: The customer called our unified commerce claim 'a diagram' and asked for the return steps, while their own phrases ('one system for the tills and the website', 'one customer, one basket', 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other') are what they were asking us to promise.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: Talk to a retailer who runs tills and web on us. For retail buyers, offer a reference call with a store-and-online retailer, a live demo of an online order returned at a till, and a rollout plan with dates, who installs and what happens to the old tills.
changes.why: The customer asked 'can I talk to them?' and wanted a live return and a rollout plan, and we answered with a case study and a description, while Adyen reportedly came with retail references Angela already knew.

changes.change: For retail and multi-store buyers: 'We name who runs your rollout, how stores get installed, and who is on call when a store goes live. One accountable vendor, not a partner you have to chase.' Use it in place of any 'we'd bring in a partner' answer, and make sure the named rollout owner and install model are real before using it.
changes.why: The 'we'd bring in a partner' answer to who does the installs met the customer's fear of two vendors pointing at each other, while Adyen came with a retail team that had done store rollouts and one contract.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For retail buyers whose pain is in stores, stop leading with global infrastructure. Open with the moment the COO watched: an online order comes back to a store and the till can't see it, and the new loyalty program splits one customer into two records. Aim this opener at the operations executive who owns the outcome, not only the technical evaluator.
changes.why: The pain was a store-floor failure seen first-hand by the COO, who signed, while our contact was the CTO running the RFP, so a global-infrastructure opener doesn't speak to the person who felt it.
